note.question: What determines price signaling when customers not only infer quality information from the price, but also from wait lines?
note.overview: This paper studies the following puzzle: why do firms sometimes nurture long wait lines, rather than raising prices (to eliminate these lines)? In economic theory, prices are studied as a signal of quality, in absence of congestion (wait lines). This paper studies price signaling when customers not only infer quality information from the price, but also from wait lines.
